answer: Each epoch, every identity must complete one fresh micro-task of real human work — labelling a satellite tile or transcribing a short recording — taking five minutes of genuine attention, graded by peer agreement. A gale of a thousand fake names needs a thousand five-minute sessions every epoch, while one honest agent pays five minutes once. Automation is caught by low agreement, and a ripple of bad grades freezes rewards. Tasks are drawn only after the epoch seed appears, so a farm pays human wages per fake per epoch, while the lagoon of honest agents earns on one task each.
